newsitem.title: DUBAI: Shell Oman says Muscat listing plans progressing.
newsitem.headline: Shell Oman says Muscat listing plans progressing.

text.p: Shell Marketing Oman Ltd's plans to float at least 40 percent of its shares on the Muscat Securities Market are progressing well and should be finalised within about two months, its general manager Tim Ford said on Monday.
"We plan to go public with the company. The details are still being worked out and should be resolved in six to eight weeks," Ford told Reuters by telephone from Muscat.
"It is a complex process floating an existing business, but we are moving in that direction."
"We will float at least 40 percent," he added.

Shell Marketing Oman Ltd is wholly owned by the Royal Dutch Shell group. It sells fuels and lubricants from over 115 service stations and also has aviation refuelling facilities in the Gulf Arab state.

Ford said the flotation would exclude Shell's upstream and downstream oil and gas operations in Oman -- its 34 percent of Petroleum Development Oman, the country's largest oil operator, and its 30 percent of Oman LNG, created to handle the downstream part of the country's huge gas project.
